classification.difficultyReason: Model present and future ages with two pronumerals, accounting for both ages increasing by 14 years.

content.prompt:
Solve by introducing two pronumerals and forming two simultaneous equations, even though this problem can be done more easily using one pronumeral.

Oscar is currently three times his son’s age. In 14 years’ time, he will be twice his son’s age. What is Oscar’s current age?

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be Oscar’s current age and $y$ his son’s current age, in years.

$$\begin{align*}x&=3y &&(1)\\x+14&=2(y+14) &&(2)\end{align*}$$

Substitute equation (1) into equation (2):

$$\begin{align*}3y+14&=2(y+14)\\3y+14&=2y+28\\y&=14\end{align*}$$

Substitute $y=14$ into equation (1):

$$\begin{align*}x&=3\times14\\x&=42\end{align*}$$

Oscar is $42$ years old. Check: $42=3\times14$, and in 14 years their ages will be $56$ and $28$, with $56=2\times28$.
